header: What the hospital route sends to the screen (step 51a). The backend payload and the card use the same shape.

members.name: asks
doc: Optional, one per row: I ask this question when the FIRST cell of that row is pressed (a department of the list opens its own OPD). null = not pressable.

members.name: badge
doc: I show a small badge beside the title of an answer about a DATE: Open (green), Closed (red), Not known (amber).

members.name: headline
doc: The ONE clean answer, shown FIRST, big and bold (step 57b): the value asked for ("DNB(MEDICINE)"), a Yes (green) or a No (red), a name, a count. I turn the title under it into a small caption.

members.name: status
doc: I keep the verdict to one line: open / closed / not known / information.

members.name: highlight
doc: The ONE thing the person most wants to see after a No (when is he available / when does the unit sit): I show an eye-catching banner for it right under the verdict.

members.name: prompt
doc: The question that the buttons under the card answer (I show it last, above the buttons).

members.name: lines
doc: Short points, shown as bullets under the table; I keep only the important words.

members.name: suggestion
doc: A helpful pointer that I show in its own box, for example the Emergency Department when the OPD is closed; one point per line (separated by a line break).

members.name: extraTables
doc: I can add more tables under the first, each with a caption (for example "Sitting on Tuesday, 27 October 2026").

members.name: details
doc: Longer explanations that I fold away until the person asks (one <details> line each): the rule behind an answer, a long list of names (step 57b).

members.name: notes
doc: Points that I show in red bullets at the foot: the OPD and card registration hours, a doctor who has retired ...

symbols.name: HospitalResult
doc: The engine returns a plain-text summary (the payload's `answer`) and the card.

members.name: ask
doc: I set this when the name fits several doctors: the app ASKS which one (radio buttons, mode "one") instead of showing the card. It is the same ask the department question uses.
